pr_title: PipeReader.CopyToAsync(Stream) should not perform zero-length writes
pr_body:
Fix https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/85733

Test for empty buffers in `CopyToAsyncCore` - do not invoke the write callback if empty

issue_context.title: PipeReader.CopyToAsync(Stream) sometimes does a zero length write
comments:
> This can be a problem if the Stream is only expecting a certain amount of data before automatically closing

I'm not following this part.  Why would calling it with 0 bytes be a problem for this?

A Content-Length response marks the stream as disposed after sending the expected number of bytes. Future writes fail with ODE. We could decide to add a check for 0-length writes before checking for disposal, but PipeReader.CopyToAsync should check the length too.
I'm happy to submit fixes for both the BCL copy and the aspnet-specific flaky zero-length write

review_comments: Do you actually need to override this?  It exists only to call something in itself that will nop.
